Model-robust dose-response modelling

Source: R/mrdrm.R
mrdrm.Rd

Combines a parametric dose-response curve fitted by drm() with a non-parametric local-linear regression (loess) fit. The fitted response is a weighted average of the two curves. When lambda contains more than one value, the function selects the weight that minimizes a prediction-error criterion; this reduces reliance on a single parametric curve shape when that shape may be misspecified. The result is intended as a complementary, model-robust fit, not as a replacement for the interpretable parameters of the parametric drm() fit.

Usage

mrdrm(
  object1,
  object2,
  lambda = (0:10)/10,
  criterion = c("gcv", "lcv"),
  critFct = c("ls", "ll"),
  ls.weights = c("nonpar", "ad hoc", "none", "par", "response"),
  fixedEnd = FALSE,
  unitScale = FALSE
)

Arguments

object1

A single-curve model fitted by drm(), with type = "continuous" or type = "binomial".

object2

An optional degree-1 loess fit to the same response and dose data. If omitted, one is fitted using the formula and data stored in object1.

lambda

Numeric candidate mixing weights between 0 and 1, inclusive. The combined fit is (1 - lambda) * object1 + lambda * object2, so 0 is purely parametric and 1 is purely local-linear. A single value fixes the weight and skips selection; multiple values are compared using criterion.

criterion

Prediction-error criterion used to select lambda: "gcv" for generalized cross-validation or "lcv" for leave-one-dose- level-out cross-validation. With a single lambda, no criterion is evaluated.

critFct

Criterion function: "ls" for least squares or "ll" for binomial log-likelihood. Continuous fits always use least squares.

ls.weights

Weighting scheme for the least-squares cross-validation criterion on binomial data: "nonpar" (weights from local-linear predictions), "par" (weights from parametric predictions), "response" (weights from observed proportions), "ad hoc" (a boundary-adjusted scheme), or "none". This argument does not affect continuous fits.

fixedEnd

If TRUE, use observed mean responses at the smallest and largest dose levels for the local-linear leave-one-dose-out predictions. This tends to favor the non-parametric component at the endpoints.

unitScale

If TRUE, refit the local-linear regression using dose values rescaled to the unit interval. Any supplied object2 is replaced by this internally fitted regression. This option cannot be combined with leave-one-dose-out selection.

Value

An object of class "mrdrc", containing the selected lambda, the combined fitted values, goodness-of-fit summaries, and both component models. Use predict() for predictions and ED() for effective-dose estimates.

Details

Use this function when the parametric model is scientifically reasonable but its exact shape is uncertain, or as a sensitivity analysis alongside the parametric fit. Effective doses for the resulting fit are obtained by inverse regression with ED().

Only single-curve continuous and binomial drm() fits are supported. Continuous fits always use least squares. For binomial fits, least squares or a binomial log-likelihood can be used. The cross-validation criterion leaves out one dose level at a time (all replicate observations at that dose), rather than one individual observation.

References

Nottingham, S. F. and Birch, C. P. D. (2000). A semi-parametric approach to analysing dose-response data. Environmental and Ecological Statistics, 7, 85-100.

See also

drm(), ED(), predict()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(ryegrass)
fit <- drm(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, fct = LL.4())
robustFit <- mrdrm(fit)
robustFit$lambda
#> [1] 0
ED(robustFit, c(10, 50, 90), display = FALSE)
# }
